slides.title: First Laval home? Know these 5 money tools.
slides.sub: The savings accounts and tax credits first-time buyers ask me about.

photo.credit: Photo: Guilhem Vellut, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: Start with a real Laval price
slides.body: Your savings plan starts with the price. Condo medians shift by sector, so compare the ones you like.

slides.title: The FHSA: save tax-free

photo.credit: Photo: Natthager, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Up to **$8,000 a year**, **$40,000 lifetime**. Contributions are generally deductible; qualifying home withdrawals aren't taxed.

slides.title: The Home Buyers' Plan (RRSP)
slides.body: First withdrawals from 2026 to 2028 start repayment in the fifth year after. You repay your RRSP over time.

slides.title: Québec's new credit: up to $1,400

photo.credit: Photo: Jean-Philippe Boulet, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: **Refundable**, starting with the 2026 tax year. Advance payments can be requested from October 2026.

slides.title: The federal Home Buyers' Amount
slides.body: A non-refundable credit. Ask your accountant how each of these fits your situation before you file.
